title: Buying an apartment with cash: cash limits in 2026
seoTitle: Buying an apartment with cash: limits in 2026
description: How much cash you can pay for an apartment in 2026: the 1,305,000 lei threshold, the 200,000 lei cash component, and the 25 percent fines.
descriptionLlm: How much cash you can pay for an apartment in 2026: the 1,305,000 lei threshold, the 200,000 lei cash component, and the 25 percent fines waiting for you.
keywords: cumparare apartament cu banii jos, plati cash imobiliare, limita numerar tranzactie imobiliara, prag 1.305.000 lei, amenda plata cash imobil, transfer bancar apartament
lead: Generations of buyers have carried apartment money in briefcases, counting banknotes by their own rules. Starting January 1, 2026, the rule belongs to the law and ties to the average national salary. With the forecasted average for 2026 at 17,400 lei, you can pay for a property entirely in cash only up to 1,305,000 lei, the equivalent of 75 average salaries. Above this amount, the apartment can no longer be bought from a briefcase. The question is not whether you can still buy with cash, but where the limit lies. The answer rests in three figures, 10,000, 200,000, and 1,305,000 lei, and in a 25 percent fine that accompanies them. Below we take them one by one, along with the journey of money through the bank.

sections.h2: The full cash threshold stands at 1,305,000 lei

blocks.x: The 2026 rule divides properties based on a ratio of 75 average salaries, with the forecasted average for this year at 17,400 lei per month. Multiply the two figures and you reach 1,305,000 lei. Up to this value, you can pay for the apartment entirely in banknotes. Beyond it, this option disappears from the discussion and the bank steps in. When comparing listings, you also look at apartment prices, because the threshold tells you right from the start whether cash remains an option for the property you want.

For you, the calculation starts with the listing price. You compare it to the threshold and immediately know whether you are negotiating a full payment in banknotes or a combination where the bank covers the lion's share.

sections.h2: Above the threshold, the bank takes over and cash stops at 200,000 lei

blocks.x: For properties that exceed 75 average salaries, the law requires payment via bank transfer. Cash does not disappear completely. You are still allowed a cash component capped at 200,000 lei, while the rest of the amount must travel through the bank. If the difference exceeds the liquid cash in your account, this is usually where the discussion about a mortgage loan comes in, which you should have long before reaching the notary's desk.
A cash component of 200,000 lei must be justified and documented. Keep the paperwork showing the origin of the money, because at the first sign of questions, it will speak on your behalf.

sections.h2: A 25 percent fine and confiscation as a package

blocks.x: The sanctions are written in Law no. 70/2015, updated by GEO no. 98/2023 and GEO no. 115/2023, and they come in two steps. You pay a fine of 25 percent of the amount exceeding the limit, and tax authorities can confiscate what you paid over the limit. Example: the permitted cash for an expensive property stops at 200,000 lei, and you hand over 250,000 lei. Out of the 50,000 lei extra, one quarter, meaning 12,500 lei, turns into a fine, and the entire amount given over the limit risks confiscation.

sections.h2: Payment in installments seems discreet and carries the same penalty

blocks.x: Payment in installments seems like a discreet way out: smaller amounts, each below the threshold, nothing put on paper. However, the law catches this arrangement as well. Fragmentation done to bypass the limits is penalized with a 25 percent fine on the split amount. You can repeat 10,000 lei installments as much as you want, but the fine will still reach 25 percent of the total cash handed over.

sections.h2: Under 10,000 lei, cash remains the simplest path

blocks.x: Law no. 70/2015 is not limited to expensive properties. It sets the general cash limit at 10,000 lei for individuals and 5,000 lei for legal entities. Below this level, paying cash remains the simplest and fastest option, without extra paperwork and without banking detours. Above it, you send the money through the bank, and for a cash component larger than 10,000 lei, you prepare justifications and documents.

In apartment transactions, the difference shows at the down payment and the small expenses you need besides the price. A small down payment can be handed over in cash without hassle, while one above the limit goes through the bank, with the statement kept in the apartment file.

sections.h2: Confirm the threshold at the notary before signing

blocks.x: The 1,305,000 lei cap starts from an average salary forecast, and forecasts get revised. You can find out the valid limit on the transaction date from the notary or the real estate agency with a phone call made before signing day. They will confirm how much cash you can bring, how much must go through the bank, and what documents to prepare for the cash portion. Have this discussion well in advance, because on the authentication day the money is already on the table and you need to know from the start how much to bring in cash and how much to leave for the bank.

faq.q: Up to what amount can I pay for an apartment entirely in cash in 2026?
faq.a: The threshold stands at 1,305,000 lei, the equivalent of 75 average salaries, with the forecasted average for 2026 at 17,400 lei. Below this value, full cash payment remains available. Above it, the transaction goes through the bank, and cash handed over stops at 200,000 lei. Because the cap ties to the average salary, the figure can shift from year to year, so confirm it with the notary or real estate agency before signing.

faq.q: What are the risks if I exceed the amount I can pay in cash?
faq.a: Law no. 70/2015, updated by GEO no. 98/2023 and GEO no. 115/2023, provides a fine of 25 percent of the exceeded amount, and tax authorities can confiscate what you paid above the limit. The same fine applies when you split the payment into installments to bypass the limits.

faq.q: Can the apartment down payment be paid in cash?
faq.a: Up to 10,000 lei, yes, which is the legal cap for individuals. Above that, you send it through the bank and keep the document.
